metaDescription: Curated investment strategies as templates for the screener: Value, Growth, Dividend Growth, Quality, Momentum and Contrarian.
title: Investment strategies
intro: Curated templates for the screener. Each card explains a strategy, lists typical criteria and links directly into the pre-configured screener. Not investment advice.

value.label: Value
value.description: Quality companies trading at a discount with a solid balance sheet. Goal: buy stocks below intrinsic value and wait for the market to re-rate them to fair value.
value.bullet4: Stress-test depth in the DCF calculator (implied growth)
value.historical: Historically a modest premium across equity cycles, but with long stretches of underperformance (e.g. 2010–2020).
value.risks: Value traps: cheap because the business model is dying. Always check quality and moat.

dividend-growth.label: Dividend Growth
dividend-growth.description: Companies with a long track record of growing dividends, a robust payout ratio and rising free cash flow. Focus on income plus capital appreciation.
dividend-growth.bullet2: At least 5–10 years of uninterrupted dividend increases
dividend-growth.historical: Smaller drawdowns than the broad market and more stable returns. Reinvested dividends compound the effect.
dividend-growth.risks: Rate-sensitive (high-yield stocks fall when rates rise). Dividend cuts during recessions.

growth.label: Quality Growth
growth.description: Companies with above-average revenue and earnings growth, high margins and a defensive balance sheet — but not at extreme valuations (GARP = Growth at a Reasonable Price).
growth.historical: Strong outperformance during low-rate regimes, deeper drawdowns during market corrections.
growth.risks: High valuation → limited cushion if growth disappoints. Momentum can flip quickly.

momentum.label: Momentum
momentum.description: Stocks that have risen sharply over recent months tend to keep rising — until the trend breaks. Combined with volume confirmation and trend quality.
momentum.historical: A well-documented factor (Jegadeesh & Titman, 1993). Pronounced out- and underperformance cycles.
momentum.risks: Short reversals can hurt. Adds significant volatility to the portfolio.

contrarian.label: Contrarian / Oversold
contrarian.description: Quality companies trading near their 52-week low — often after an exaggerated reaction to quarterly results or sector news. Requires patience and research.
contrarian.bullet3: Due diligence: balance sheet, cash flow, management commentary
contrarian.historical: Origin of modern value strategies (DeBondt/Thaler). Strong rebounds are possible but real zombies exist too.
contrarian.risks: Value traps are most dangerous here. Always run at least a bull/bear analysis plus conviction score.

defensive.label: Defensive Blue Chips
defensive.description: Large-cap companies with non-cyclical business models (consumer staples, healthcare, utilities), a low beta and a robust dividend. The calm core of a portfolio.
defensive.historical: Low volatility and steady performance. Underperforms in bull markets, provides protection in bear markets.
defensive.risks: Rate-sensitive (utilities). Limited growth story — total return comes mostly from dividends.
